fatal_errors: The proposed Al-Sc alloy is unrelated to the target random bcc HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy.

The response predicts reduced conductivity from precipitate scattering, whereas the target result is an approximately 12% increase caused by SRO-induced reduction of lattice distortion and high-conductivity percolation pathways.
It replaces simulated chemical short-range ordering and HfTi/TiZr clustering with an unsupported aging treatment and Sc-rich precipitates.
Using pure Al as the baseline does not isolate the effect of ordering or precipitates from alloying and composition effects.
Flash measurements of total thermal conductivity in metallic Al-Sc do not isolate lattice thermal conductivity, which is strongly confounded by electronic heat transport.
The numerical treatment conditions, precipitate sizes, and 20% conductivity decrease are asserted without cited evidence.
explanation: The hypothesis only shares the broad topic of precipitate-related phonon scattering. It misses the target material, atomistic simulation conditions, SRO structures, percolative mechanism, random-alloy baseline, and the direction and magnitude of the outcome. Its falsification experiment could test total conductivity in Al-Sc, but it cannot adequately test a lattice-conductivity claim without separating electronic and phononic contributions. With no supporting evidence and several invented quantitative details, it is unsupported rather than a reconstruction.
